packs.title: Lake, Hills and Looking Closely
packs.promise: Compare transport, rock, architecture and views across four separate Lucerne outings.

q.s: Build a three-object comparison of how people and things travel.
st: Enter via the signed museum visitor entrance from the Lidostrasse approach with valid museum admission and applicable fee or entitlement: adult CHF37, under-26 student or apprentice CHF27 with proof, under-16 CHF16, under-6 free. Valid IV proof gives 10% off and an eligible assistance companion free admission; other reductions have separate terms and do not combine. The museum exhibition halls and Media World open daily 10:00–18:00 from 29 March–24 October 2026, and 10:00–17:00 from 25 October 2026–27 March 2027; check the published calendar for other dates. Allow 15–25 min for entry.

Spend a focused two hours finding three actually displayed transport objects with different jobs. For each, record one visible shape and the use explained by its label. Choose ordinary open displays; no simulator, performance or extra ticket is needed.
Compare which design choice most clearly serves its job. Write a three-row record: object, visible clue, labelled function. Separate your interpretation from the label’s explanation.
Leave time to exit normally. The next longer public-street and stair route to Dreilinden is 2.5 km / 40 mapped min with roughly 110 m ascent; allow 55–65 min and follow public pedestrian signs.

q.s: Compose the view in three layers, then change the foreground.
st: After the museum, use the longer street route via Haldenstrasse, Zinggentor, Haldensteig, Adligenswilerstrasse, Abendweg and the Steigerweg stairs toward Dreilinden. Allow 55–65 min for the measured 2.5 km / 40 min ascent and finding the signed public pedestrian gate. Do not use the rejected private shortcut or pass a closed gate.

Inside the open public park, find a safe path-side view. Park hours are 08:00–22:00 but paths are unlit; keep this visit in daylight. Spend a few minutes selecting an actual foreground, middle distance and far line.

Make an original three-layer arrangement in words or a quick sketch. Change only the foreground and write how that changes the balance. No particular weather, mountain visibility or flower display is required.

Return by the open signed pedestrian exit and Steigerweg stair route toward town. Budget 40–50 min for the measured 2 km / 28 min descent to Bahnhof; use actual signs and stop if wet, icy or closed access makes the route unsuitable.

q.s: Separate what stone shows you from what a label explains.
st: Find the signed Kassenhaus ticket building, distinct from the Schweizerhaus and Felsenwelt. Allow 15 min for finding it and 15 min for admission after the memorial. Use applicable admission: 16+ CHF24, apprentices, students, AHV or IV CHF18, ages 6–15 CHF12, under 6 free; valid Swiss Museum Pass or Raiffeisen MemberPlus free. Claim pass or Visitor Card reductions at the cashier with required proof.
Spend 90 min in the open glacial pothole area and its interpretation. For three features, first write a physical observation: shape, surface or relative position.
Read the nearest relevant interpretation and add a separate explanation beside each observation. Mark any point the label does not establish as your own question, not a fact.

Compare which feature was hardest to interpret by sight alone. Exit before closing and return via the observed Denkmalstrasse park mouth and Löwenplatz toward Bahnhof: 1.2 km / 16 min mapped, with 25 min allowed after a 10 min normal exit allowance.

packs.title: The River and the Wall
packs.promise: Follow river structures and climb through the wall to the Old Town squares.

q.s: Find three interior details without breaking the room’s quiet.
st: At Jesuit Church, check signs and the current calendar for worship, concerts or closures. Ordinary visitor admission is free, normally until 18:30; Monday and Thursday opens 09:30, other days 06:30. Do not enter for sightseeing during a service or event. Allow 5–10 min for checking and quiet entry.

During a quiet 30 min visit, find one stucco detail, one support or column detail and one effect of natural or interior light. Observe from normal visitor positions without touching or rearranging anything.
Write where each detail sits and how two of them work together visually. Keep your note brief and your voice low; no photograph or music performance is needed.
Leave normally and follow the open southern riverside route via Reusssteg and Pfistergasse toward Spreuer Bridge: 350 m / 4 min mapped, with 8 min allowed.

q.s: Turn the bridge’s change of direction into an original six-mark response.
st: On the open public Spreuer walkway, choose a safe place clear of pedestrian flow. Notice where the two bridge sections meet at a bend, and compare a roof line with a support rhythm.

Make an original six-mark response in your own notebook: two marks for the bend, two for the supports and two for the roof. Words can stand in for marks if you prefer; do not trace or copy the historic paintings.
Change one mark and explain how it changes the sense of movement. Your response need not be a realistic picture or a historical claim.
Cross the open bridge normally toward Mühlenplatz. Allow 5 min for the measured 190 m / 3 min connection, which includes stairs; stop for writing only where people can pass safely.

q.s: Write a colour address that another person could picture.
st: At Weinmarkt, use an open public position away from entrances and walking lines. The measured Hirschenplatz link is 47 m / about 1 min, with 5 min allowed to reposition.

Select three colours you can actually see on built surfaces and one spatial relationship, such as above, beside or between. Locate them precisely enough to distinguish your view from a generic square.
Write an original two-sentence “address in colour” without a building name: a small composition someone could picture. Replace one colour or relationship and explain which version is clearer.
Continue along the open public route toward Kornmarkt, 120 m / 2 min measured; allow 5 min. No current market, flower display or fountain operation is needed for either task.
